tour.overview:
Pisa was a great sea power in the 11th and 12th centuries, and it spent its wealth on a cathedral complex so beautiful that the meadow around it became known as the Field of Miracles. Work on the bell tower began in 1173, and the soft ground started to give way after the third storey. The builders kept going, bending the upper floors to compensate, and the tower has leaned ever since; engineers stabilised it between 1990 and 2001. The Piazza dei Miracoli has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987. Half an hour away, Lucca stayed an independent republic until Napoleon's time and is still enclosed by massive 16th- and 17th-century walls, now a park shaded by plane trees.

This private day combines the photo everyone wants with the town many visitors fall in love with. In the morning your guide shows you Pisa's cathedral, Baptistery and tower, with time to climb it if you wish. After lunch in Lucca, you walk or cycle along the walls, see the Roman amphitheatre turned into a square, the churches of San Michele and San Martino and the tower with a garden on top.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Florence, or the cruise port of Livorno
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; about 5 km on flat ground, or by bicycle in Lucca

WHAT YOU SEE
• Pisa: the Leaning Tower, the cathedral, the Baptistery and the Camposanto (outside).
• Lucca: the city walls, Piazza dell'Anfiteatro, San Michele in Foro, the cathedral of San Martino and the Guinigi Tower.

WHY THIS WORKS
We arrive in Pisa early, before the cruise and coach groups, and give Lucca the relaxed afternoon it deserves, instead of the hurried hour most tours allow.

WHO IT SUITS
Families, cruise passengers in Livorno, cyclists and anyone who wants an easy, flat day in Tuscany.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer wine and hill towns, choose our Chianti, San Gimignano and Siena day trip.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The tower climb has about 250 steps and is not allowed for children under 8. Tower tickets are timed and limited; we book them with your request. Bags must be left in the cloakroom before climbing.

days.name: Pisa's Field of Miracles, lunch in Lucca, the city walls and the old town of Lucca
days.description:
What to expect: Pisa's famous tower and the walled city of Lucca in a relaxed day, with a licensed guide, private car, lunch and an optional tower climb.

Your driver collects you at your Florence hotel at about 8:15, or at the cruise terminal in Livorno, and takes you to Pisa in about an hour. Your guide meets you at the gate of the Piazza dei Miracoli, the green lawn where white marble buildings seem to float. You start with the cathedral, begun in 1063 with the spoils of a naval victory, its façade of arcades setting the style that became known as Pisan Romanesque. Inside, under a gilded ceiling, stand Giovanni Pisano's carved pulpit and the bronze lamp said to have given Galileo, born in Pisa in 1564, his ideas about the pendulum.

You walk around the round Baptistery, the largest in Italy, famous for its echo, and come to the tower itself. Your guide explains how it began to lean, why it never fell and how engineers straightened it by about 40 centimetres by removing soil from under its north side. If you have chosen the climb, you take your timed slot up the worn spiral staircase to the bells, with views over the red roofs to the mountains. Otherwise, there is time for the classic photo.

At about 12:30 you drive to Lucca, 30 minutes away. After lunch in the old town – tordelli pasta, farro soup or chestnut-flour cake – you climb onto the walls, four kilometres around and wide enough for an avenue of trees. You can walk a section with your guide or rent bicycles for a full loop, about 25 minutes of easy riding. Back in the streets, you see the oval Piazza dell'Anfiteatro, where houses were built over the seats of a Roman arena, the white façade of San Michele in Foro, the cathedral of San Martino with its carved labyrinth, and the Guinigi Tower, crowned by holm oaks. Your driver takes you back to Florence or the port at about 16:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:15 – Pick-up at your hotel in Florence (or at Livorno port).
09:15 – Piazza dei Miracoli: cathedral, Baptistery and tower.
11:00 – Optional climb of the Leaning Tower.
12:00 – Drive to Lucca.
12:30 – Lunch in Lucca.
14:00 – The walls on foot or by bicycle.
15:00 – Old town: Piazza dell'Anfiteatro, San Michele, San Martino, Guinigi Tower.
16:00 – Drive back.
17:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The tower climb must be booked in advance for a fixed time; children under 8 are not allowed and those under 18 must be with an adult.
• Lucca hosts the Puccini Festival in summer and the Comics festival in late October, when the town is very busy.
• Cruise passengers: we plan to have you back at the ship at least one hour before all-aboard time.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Pisa Cathedral ticket, lunch, bottled water, pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: Leaning Tower climb (can be added), bicycle rental in Lucca, drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is the climb of the Leaning Tower included?
faq.answer: It is optional, because not everyone wants to climb about 250 steps. Tell us when you book and we will reserve your timed slot and add the ticket to the price.

faq.question: Can children climb the tower?
faq.answer: Children under 8 are not allowed to climb, and anyone under 18 must be with an adult. Younger children can enjoy the square and the Baptistery's echo.

faq.question: Can you pick us up from the cruise ship in Livorno?
faq.answer: Yes. Pisa is about 30 minutes from the port. We plan the day so you are back at least one hour before the ship's all-aboard time.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes, Pisa Cathedral. The Baptistery, the Camposanto, the tower climb and the Guinigi Tower can be added.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, lunch at a local restaurant in Lucca. Vegetarian, gluten-free and other diets can be arranged.

faq.question: Can we cycle on Lucca's walls?
faq.answer: Yes, it is one of the nicest things to do in Tuscany. Bicycles, including tandems and child seats, are rented at the foot of the walls for a small fee paid locally.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Yes, largely. Both towns are flat, the Piazza dei Miracoli and Lucca's walls have ramps, and the car can drop you close to the sights. The tower climb is not accessible.

faq.question: Will we be taken to souvenir shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: Can we add Florence or Cinque Terre?
faq.answer: Pisa and Lucca fit well with a half day in Florence for cruise passengers. Cinque Terre is a separate full day; ask us for a custom plan.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes and, for the cathedral, clothes covering shoulders and knees.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year. Spring and autumn are ideal for cycling the walls; summer mornings in Pisa can be hot and crowded, which is why we start early.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
